checks.result: The raw 8 MiB check precedes JSONDecoder. The duplicate-key scanner is reached only after successful envelope decoding. Returning at root close relies on the decoder having validated the remaining input; no independent permissive parsing path was found.

checks.result: Two-byte escape skipping preserves quote boundaries for already-valid JSON. Only commas in the current object scope reset expectsKey; array commas do not affect the parent object. Closing scopes release their key sets. No concrete lexical scope defect identified.

cases: direct ASCII key versus equivalent Unicode escape
direct scalar versus escaped surrogate pair
UTF-16/UTF-32 BOM precedence and BOM-free ASCII structural prefixes
checks.result: Keys are decoded as JSON strings before exact UTF-8 Data comparison, which identifies equivalent escape spellings without intentionally normalizing canonically equivalent but distinct sequences. UTF-32 BOM detection precedes UTF-16 detection; prefix tests are coherent for object or JSON-whitespace starts. Runtime behavior was not executed.

The imported raw byte count is bounded. Scanner traversal is iterative; scope storage grows with nesting and stored key data, and sets are mutated in place then released at scope close. There is no application-defined depth ceiling in this file. UTF conversion and decoder/scanner allocations mean the raw-byte limit is not a measured peak-memory guarantee. No crash or unbounded-loop case established from source.

Definitions reject raw numeric overflow/nonfinite values, malformed or noninteger version tokens, invalid UTF-8, unpaired surrogates, a NUL-containing name, and an extra JSON root. Positive controls preserve valid equivalent integer spellings and an escaped surrogate pair. These methods were read, not run.
